- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}

Better: combine: A "rabbit hutch" sort puzzle with levels, move one rabbit at a time between hutches; only move if destination empty or top rabbit same color; win when every hutch is monochrome or empty. Add undo, restart, hints? Levels procedurally generated with guarantee solvability. Nice animations, hopping rabbit sprites (CSS/SVG), sound via WebAudio, confetti on win.

Visual design: cozy meadow, wooden burrows, rabbits drawn with CSS/SVG. Each rabbit could be an SVG with body, ears, face, tail; color palettes. Sorting puzzle: 5-7 burrows, each capacity 4. Rabbits visible stacked.

Could also make it less abstract: rabbits sit in colored "Häschen-Gehege" and you tap a rabbit then a hutch to move. Top rabbit only? For sort puzzle, matching rule makes it strategic. But requirement just "sort rabbits by color"; a free-form version where you can move any rabbit to any hutch, winning when sorted, is easier and more intuitive. With capacity and one-at-a-time, it's still puzzle but no fail states. Could have levels increasing colors.

Let me create a mobile-friendly game with:
- Start screen / level select maybe.
- 12 handcrafted levels (from easy 3 colors to 8 colors) plus endless generated.
- Tap hutch to pick top rabbit; tap another hutch to place. Allowed if destination has space; if non-empty top must match color. Standard and understandable with tutorial.

- Move counter, timer, best saved in localStorage.
- Win overlay with stars based on moves?

Need to ensure solvability: generate by reverse moves from solved state, or shuffle deck among hutches (like ball sort generators). Reverse-move generation is safest. Generate solved state with N colors x 4 rabbits, plus 2 empty hutches, then perform random legal reverse "unmoves"? In ball sort, reverse of a legal move: moving top rabbit(s) from a completed/any stack to another where they came from. Actually easier: random shuffle distribute colors into hutches then test solvability via BFS/DFS solver. For up to 7 colors × 4 = 28 plus 2 empty, BFS could be huge but with 9 hutches capacity 4, a DFS solver might work. Generated random distribution is usually solvable (ball sort puzzles generally are), but not guaranteed. I can implement a solver with memo and backtracking; for random deals, should find solution quickly usually. Or do reverse generation:

Forward legal move rule: pop top rabbit from source (must be top), place on destination if dest empty or top color matches, dest not full.
Reverse: from a state, move top rabbit from a stack to another stack where source? Reverse of move src->dst placing color c on matching top. In reverse, moving a rabbit from a stack to another is always a legal forward move in the other direction if destination (original src) top matches or is empty after? Hmm reverse move is valid if in the original forward move, the rabbit was taken from src (top) and put on dst. In reverse, we take the top rabbit from dst and put it back on src. Solver implementation:
```
function key(stacks) {
  return stacks.map(s=>s.join(',')).sort().join('|');
}
function solve(stacks, cap, maxNodes=200000) {
  const seen = new Set();
  let nodes=0;
  const path=[];
  function dfs(st) {
    if (nodes++ > maxNodes) return null;
    if (isSolved(st)) return path.slice();
    const k = key(st);
    if (seen.has(k)) return null;
    seen.add(k);
    // moves
    const moves = [];
    for i... for j... if i!==j ...
      const src=st[i], dst=st[j];
      if (!src.length || dst.length>=cap) continue;
      const c=src[src.length-1];
      if (dst.length && dst[dst.length-1]!==c) continue;
      // avoid pointless: moving complete monochrome stack to empty, moving single from mono? prune
      let score=0;
      if (dst.length && dst[dst.length-1]===c) score+=10;
      if (src.length===1) score += 3;
      if (dst.length===0) score -= 1;
      // moving entire source (all same color) to empty useless
      if (dst.length===0 && src.every(x=>x===c)) continue;
      // don't move from a stack that is already sorted and complete? If src all same and can be built further maybe allow; skip moving from monochrome stack if not needed
      moves.push({i,j,score});
    moves.sort((a,b)=>b.score-a.score);
    for (const m of moves) {
      st[m.j].push(st[m.i].pop()); path.push([m.i,m.j]);
      const r=dfs(st);
      if (r) return r;
      path.pop(); st[m.i].push(st[m.j].pop());
    }
    return null;
  }
  return dfs(stacks.map(s=>s.slice()));
}
```

## Objective
- Build a playable, polished browser game in the empty PlayGround project based on the German prompt: “In diesem Spiel musst du Hasen nach Farbe sortieren” (sort rabbits by color).

## Requirements
- User provided no explicit constraints beyond the game premise; infer a complete, mobile-friendly rabbit color-sorting game.
- Project runs as a static HTML site served by the platform’s default start script.

## Decisions
- Implemented a cozy ball-sort-style puzzle: 3 rabbits per hutch, 3–7 colors, 1–2 empty hutches, tap top rabbit then target hutch; move only to same color or empty hutch.
- Added 18 verified-solvable levels with par move counts, star ratings, hints via DFS solver, undo, restart, level select, progress persistence, sound, haptics, and confetti.
- All visuals are self-contained SVG/CSS/JS; no external assets or libraries.
- Responsive layouts: desktop one row, mobile balanced 2 rows, short-landscape one row, plus two-column landscape intro and compact landscape win modal.
- Focus rings are suppressed for pointer input but retained for keyboard navigation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `styles.css`, `game.js`, and `levels.js`.
- Generated and solver-verified 18 levels; fixed missing `colors` metadata.
- Verified all 18 levels through actual browser UI: solutions win, stars register, no console/page errors.
- Verified layouts at 1280×800, 768×1024, 390×844, 390×667, 320×568, and 844×390 with no header/control collisions or page overflow.
- Verified hint, undo, invalid-move feedback, level select, win overlay, intro modal, and landscape modal fit.
- Added `?level=N&nointro=1` query support for testing screenshots.
- Checked intro modal at 390×667: height 582px, start button visible.

### Active
